title: Exploitation for Defense Impairment
summary: This technique is not tied to one product. It describes using a software flaw in a security control as the way to weaken or remove that control. The vulnerable component is the defense itself, such as endpoint detection and response agents, antivirus drivers, edge firewall appliances, or cloud and software as a service security boundaries, and attackers commonly run discovery first to learn which of those products is present in the environment. Exploitation may run attacker code at a high privilege level, terminate the protective process, break a driver, or bypass an enforcement check. Detection rarely comes from the exploited tool, because that tool is what failed, so defenders lean on process creation around the security agent, unexpected driver or service changes, gaps in agent health and heartbeat reported to the management console, and crash or tamper alerts that the product still manages to send before it stops.

beginner.definition: This technique means attacking the security tools themselves. The attacker looks for a bug in antivirus, in an endpoint agent, or in another protection. Then they use that bug to switch the protection off. This is different from simply stopping a normal service.
beginner.whyItMatters: Security tools are the last line that catches an intruder. If an attacker can break one, the rest of the attack becomes much easier. The broken product may not report the problem, so silence is the danger. Teams that watch agent health can notice a tool that stops sending data. Patching security products quickly will close this path for attackers.
howItWorks: The attacker first lists which security products run in the environment, a step called discovery.
They look for a known bug in one of those products that they can reach.
They send crafted input to the product so that it runs their own code.
That code often runs with high rights and can stop the protective process.
The protection is now weakened or gone, and later attack steps are harder to see.
The management console may show a missing heartbeat or a crash report from the agent.
beginner.example: Think of a museum with a motion alarm in every room. A thief does not smash the display case. They find a fault in the alarm panel itself. They send the panel a strange signal, and the panel quietly switches off. The cameras still record the empty corridor for anyone who looks later. Nothing looks wrong until somebody checks the panel. Security software can fail in the same silent way, so its health matters as much as its alerts.
takeaways: Watch the health of your security tools, because a broken tool may send no alert at all.
Patch security products as quickly as you patch the systems they protect.
Treat a stopped agent as a possible attack, and not only as an outage.

objectives: Explain what it means to exploit a security product rather than a business application.
Identify the security controls that attackers most often target for impairment.
Describe how discovery of installed security software supports this technique.
Use agent health, heartbeat, and crash telemetry to detect a disabled protection.
Explain how patching and tamper protection reduce the risk from this technique.
